clusters.name: Pasar Makan @ Reservoir (Blk 630)
clusters.notes: The neighbourhood centre. Mostly a breakfast-to-lunch crowd.

clusters.name: Bedok 216 Food Centre & Market
clusters.notes: Big, busy morning centre at Bedok Town. Many stalls close by early afternoon.

clusters.name: Bedok 85 Fengshan Centre
clusters.notes: The east's supper institution — bak chor mee, BBQ and porridge into the night.

clusters.name: Kaki Bukit 511 Market & Food Centre
clusters.notes: Neighbourhood centre between Bedok North and Bedok Reservoir MRT, with plenty of evening and supper stalls.

clusters.name: Blk 538 Bedok North St 3 Market & Food Centre
clusters.notes: Neighbourhood morning centre. Mapped from a Jan 2026 guide and an online roster; details on many stalls still unconfirmed.

clusters.name: Old Airport Road Food Centre
clusters.notes: One of Singapore's biggest and most famous hawker centres — two long rows of legends. Many stalls close by mid-afternoon or on Mondays.

clusters.name: Bedok Interchange Hawker Centre (208B)
clusters.notes: Right beside Bedok MRT and bus interchange; open late, good for a quick bite on the way home.

clusters.name: Pasar 16 @ Bedok South (Blk 16)
clusters.notes: Morning-heavy neighbourhood centre; famous for Hill Street Char Kway Teow.

clusters.name: Tampines Round Market & Food Centre (Blk 137)
clusters.notes: Tampines' classic breakfast centre — most stalls close by early afternoon.

clusters.name: Hawker Centre @ Our Tampines Hub
clusters.notes: Air-conditioned-feel modern hawker centre inside the Our Tampines Hub sports & community complex; open late.

clusters.name: Pasir Ris Central Hawker Centre
clusters.notes: Two-storey newer-generation hawker centre beside Pasir Ris MRT and White Sands; lots of young hawkers.

clusters.name: Changi Village Hawker Centre
clusters.notes: A weekend trip out east — nasi lemak, beef kway teow and dessert by the sea, next to the Pulau Ubin ferry terminal.

clusters.name: Marine Parade Central Market & Food Centre
clusters.notes: Mixed Chinese and Malay neighbourhood centre; Neptune dim sum has run round the clock.

clusters.name: Haig Road Market & Food Centre
clusters.notes: Strong on Malay food — putu piring, mee rebus, soto, satay — plus kolo mee and claypot rice.

clusters.name: Geylang Serai Market & Food Centre
clusters.notes: The heart of Malay food in Singapore — upstairs food centre above the wet market. Busiest during Hari Raya.

clusters.name: Dunman Food Centre
clusters.notes: Small Joo Chiat-side centre that runs late — rojak, kway teow and zi char at night.

clusters.name: East Coast Lagoon Food Village
clusters.notes: Seaside hawker centre in East Coast Park — BBQ seafood, satay and evening breeze. Best in the evening; parking can be tight on weekends.

clusters.name: Eunos Crescent Market & Food Centre (4A)
clusters.notes: Neighbourhood centre near Eunos MRT — prata, briyani and desserts.

clusters.name: Bedok Corner Food Centre
clusters.notes: Small open-air centre at the Upper East Coast end of Bedok Road — lots of Malay food, BBQ and laksa.

clusters.name: Bedok Mall
clusters.notes: Above Bedok MRT and bus interchange. Basement 1–2 are mostly food.

clusters.name: Tampines Mall
clusters.notes: Tampines' main mall beside the MRT; restaurants spread over B1 to Level 4.

clusters.name: Tampines 1
clusters.notes: Youth-leaning mall across from Tampines MRT; strong on hotpot, grilled fish and desserts.

clusters.name: Century Square
clusters.notes: Next to Tampines MRT; Haidilao here runs till 2am.

clusters.name: Jewel Changi Airport
clusters.notes: Worth-the-trip mall around the Rain Vortex; many places open early or late. Paid parking at Jewel/T1.

clusters.name: White Sands
clusters.notes: Beside Pasir Ris MRT; kiosks in B1 for quick bites.

clusters.name: Pasir Ris Mall
clusters.notes: Newer mall at the Pasir Ris integrated hub, connected to the MRT and bus interchange.

clusters.name: Eastpoint Mall
clusters.notes: Simei's neighbourhood mall by the MRT. Has a newer food court, Hawkers' Street (opened Jun 2025), not yet mapped stall by stall.

clusters.name: Changi City Point
clusters.notes: Outlet mall by Expo MRT; family-friendly with a big basement food row.

clusters.name: Parkway Parade
clusters.notes: Marine Parade's big mall beside Marine Parade MRT; Kopitiam Food Hall in the basement.

clusters.name: i12 Katong
clusters.notes: Katong's lifestyle mall on East Coast Road. Mall open 10am–10pm.

clusters.name: Paya Lebar Quarter (PLQ)
clusters.notes: Office-and-mall precinct at Paya Lebar MRT; lots of after-work spots.

clusters.name: Paya Lebar Square
clusters.notes: Across from PLQ at Paya Lebar MRT; casual chains and mini-bowl spots.

clusters.name: SingPost Centre
clusters.notes: Above Paya Lebar MRT. Mall open 10am–10pm; Singapura Heritage food court on Level 2.

roster.snapshot: live directory (Cafes, Restaurants & Food Court + Food kiosk / Takeaway)

clusters.name: Downtown East (E!Hub & E!Avenue)
clusters.notes: Family leisure hub near Wild Wild Wet and Pasir Ris Park. Roster only (undated guide), so check before going.

clusters.name: Our Tampines Hub (shops)
clusters.notes: The restaurants, cafés and kiosks around the community hub (the hawker centre is listed separately).

roster.snapshot: live directory (F&B, accurate as of 1 Oct 2026)

clusters.name: KINEX
clusters.notes: Formerly OneKM, next to Paya Lebar MRT. Basement kiosks plus restaurants on Levels 1–2.

clusters.name: Katong V
clusters.notes: Small Far East mall on East Coast Road; cafés and restaurants on Level 1.

clusters.name: Siglap Centre
clusters.notes: Small neighbourhood mall with Cold Storage; a few fast-food outlets.

clusters.name: Djitsun Mall Bedok
clusters.notes: Small mall next to Bedok Mall and the bus interchange (Golden Village, enrichment centres). Only a handful of food outlets.

roster.snapshot: directory (Food & Dining; undated third-party site, no units)

clusters.name: Plaza Singapura
clusters.notes: Above Dhoby Ghaut MRT. Food is mostly in B1–B2 and level 1.

clusters.name: Raffles City
clusters.notes: Linked to City Hall MRT. Basement food court and restaurants on B1–L3.

clusters.name: Funan
clusters.notes: Lifestyle mall near City Hall; cafés and restaurants on B2–L3.

clusters.name: Bugis Junction
clusters.notes: Above Bugis MRT. Food on B1 and level 3.

clusters.name: Bugis+
clusters.notes: Across the link bridge from Bugis Junction; restaurants on the upper floors.

clusters.name: Junction 8
clusters.notes: Bishan's main mall, next to Bishan MRT and bus interchange.

clusters.name: Clarke Quay
clusters.notes: Riverside dining blocks; bars-only and nightclubs left out.

clusters.name: The Centrepoint
clusters.notes: Orchard Road, near Somerset MRT.

clusters.name: Tiong Bahru Plaza
clusters.notes: Above Tiong Bahru MRT; food court and restaurants on B1–L2.

clusters.name: Lau Pa Sat
clusters.notes: Victorian cast-iron market (national monument), privately run, so not on NEA's list. Several stalls open 24 hours. Satay Street on Boon Tat Street opens in the evening.

clusters.name: Amoy Street Food Centre
clusters.address: 7 Maxwell Road (National Development Bldg Annex B), S069111
clusters.notes: Two floors of CBD lunch favourites. Many stalls are weekday-lunch only and close by 2:30–3pm.

clusters.name: Maxwell Food Centre
clusters.notes: Chinatown's famous centre (Tian Tian chicken rice). Busy with tourists; open most of the day.

clusters.name: Market Street Hawker Centre
clusters.notes: Reopened in CapitaSpring in 2022 (56 stalls, levels 2–3; NEA's 2024 list still shows 76 at the old Golden Shoe site). Mostly weekday breakfast and lunch.
